newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed after volatile session.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed after a volatile session that saw the July contract trade in a 14-cent range.
Traders said July was still prone to wide price fluctuations amid ongoing assessments of the damage to the U.S. HRW wheat crop as a result of a freeze April 12-13 in the central and southern Plains.

May wheat gained Tuesday on a technical bounce tied to signals that Monday's sell-off was overdone. But May also gained relative to July on ideas that few deliveries will be made against the May contract, traders said.
The May/July spread had narrowed in recent days but widened Tuesday to settle at 13 cents after opening at nine cents.

"The function of the spread this close to delivery is either to fuel the belief that deliveries will be made or alleviate fears of deliveries," a KCBT trader said. "The recent narrowing of the May/July spread allowed traders to roll their position at a more 'advantageous' discount."
KCBT wheat settled one cent per bushel lower to 3-1/2 cents higher, with May up 3-1/2 cents at $4.52-1/2. July lost one cent to close at $4.40.

Traders said commodity brokerage Benson-Quinn, which bear-spread at least 3.5 million July/May on Monday, was again a featured bear-spreader, doing 2.5 million of the July/May spread at nine to 13 cents per bushel.
Refco sold 1.4 million July bushels. Wolcott Lincoln bull-spread 1.8 million May/July at between nine and 13 cents.
